analysis.title: Market Review & Outlook: Fiscal concerns add to AI overspending risks
key_insights: Global markets became more volatile in October as renewed energy-price pressure and fiscal concerns weighed on risk appetite. France's political situation pushed sovereign risk premiums higher and weighed on the euro.
Brent crude rose above US$110 per barrel in October, lifting the broader commodities complex.
The 10-year US Treasury yield fell back below 5% at month-end after reaching 5.3% earlier in October, as investors moved into safe assets.
US Q3 earnings season began with mixed results from major banks. Headline profits concealed weaker fixed income trading revenues.
EM equities lagged in October, reflecting the correction in semiconductors. European high yield also posted weak performance on fiscal sustainability concerns.
The strong dollar and elevated real yields remain a challenge for precious metals.

The bank sees US growth supported by AI-related capex, resilient consumer spending and a solid labour market. It judges financial conditions not restrictive enough given persistent underlying inflation and energy-price pressure.
The bank expects the Fed to hike to 4.25% in December, with further hikes in 2027.
The bank expects the ECB to raise its deposit rate to 2.75% in December and hike once more in early 2027.

France's borrowing costs are at new highs on political instability and no credible fiscal consolidation plan. Stabilising the debt ratio would need a substantial primary balance improvement, which is politically hard before the 2027 presidential election. The bank expects this to weigh on the euro near term.
The bank expects the SNB to hike to 0.5% in the first half of 2027. It sees some UK tightening around the turn of the year.

Japan benefits from external demand, rising real wages, fiscal support and a weak yen. Underlying inflation argues for further tightening. China's activity is uneven, with strong exports against weak domestic demand and property.

The 10-year French-German government bond spread has widened to around 150 basis points. The bank favours intermediate-duration government bonds for carry and roll-down, and sees shorter French maturities as relatively attractive.
Credit spreads have widened from exceptionally tight levels, especially in lower-rated segments, but remain consistent with resilient activity.

The bank expects AI investment and earnings growth to support equities, but gains should moderate on fading macro support and higher discount rates. It favours developed over emerging markets, with a preference for the US and Switzerland. Preferred sectors are communication services (telecoms preferred), consumer staples and utilities.
Asset allocation: slight overweight equities, slight underweight bonds, slight underweight alternatives. The bank trimmed EM government bonds and added high-yield bonds.
